kind.technique: A method, with the pieces that use it.
kind.atom: A reusable part with parameters: substrate, process, texture, color, engine, field, mark, voice, space or bus.
kind.exploration: A piece that runs techniques on a subject.
kind.coupling: An exploration with one driver and named consequences.
kind.study: A reference measured and rebuilt in code, with a spec.
kind.template: A layout made for reuse with new content.
kind.document: A written piece with figures: a design document, a report, a dossier.
kind.plate: One figure isolated from a page.

status.canonical: Work that is presented as correct and finished.
status.exploration: Kept because it asks a question, not because it answers one.
status.known-failure: Shown because it fails, and the failure is the lesson.
status.unsorted: Imported from the inventory. No editorial ruling yet.
status.proposed: Written by the tool (ck-e6 candidate-technique detector). Julia rules by editing the stub.

family.print-physics: How ink meets the sheet: plates, register, coverage, bleed.
family.line: Keylines, contours, pen and brush lines.
family.screen-tone: Tone carried by dots, lines, hatch and stipple.
family.grain-stock: Grain, tooth, mottle and the sheet itself.
family.light-gradient: Gradients, ramps, blur, glow and shading.
family.fields-optics: Scalar and vector fields, simulations, optical models.
family.type: Lettering and type treated as a drawn object.
family.layout-ephemera: Cards, frames, labels and paper hardware.
family.subject-construction: Parts of one plate's drawing. Filed for the record; not liftable.
family.data-display: Charts, diagrams and readouts drawn in code.
family.pixel-sprite: Pixel scenes, sprite sheets and isometric tiles.
family.fabric: Weave, stitch and cloth: setts, twills, stitches and the threads that make them.

access.staged: Built or proposed, not yet on the site.

techniques.name: Hillshade and flow — one field, two jobs
A shader that does not link

uses.implementation: Two dashed hairline extensions drop from the object being dimensioned. A solid dimension line runs between them with a filled triangle at each end. The dimension letter (italic serif, single character) sits at the middle above the line; the formula or note (mono, low contrast) sits below.

Each apparatus chamber is a filled rectangle or shear rhomb in the neutral bench fill with a 1.4 pt ink stroke. The transmission axis of each polarizer is hatched inside the chamber — vertical for P, horizontal for A. Nothing else lives inside a chamber; every notation about a chamber sits outside it.

Every geometric relationship the picture needs but the object does not embody is drawn once as a hairline in the low-contrast neutral. The optical axis runs the full plate width at 1 pt and a 2-5 pitch dash so it disappears against the eye and reappears at the read head.

Two rays leave the crystal in a persistent two-key encoding: ink solid for the ordinary path, ink dashed for the extraordinary. Where the analyser recombines their components, the stroke thickens to 3 pt as a single ink line to the image plane. The plate is legible under any print or paper condition; no hue is asserted where none exists inside the crystal.

At each stage where the polarization state is knowable, a compact glyph names it — a vertical double-arrow after P, a dot-in-circle on the ordinary ray, a slanted double-arrow on the extraordinary. Each glyph carries a mono E label if the state is not obvious from context.
A single hairline rule sits below the drawing; a mono stage label rides beneath each apparatus centre, roman numeral + name. Reading the rule top-down, the bench and the process become one row.

The extraordinary ray enters the calcite at the same point as the ordinary but bends inside toward the optic axis, then leaves parallel to the entrance ray and displaced by Δ. The angle marker is a short arc at the exit; its numeric label sits above the arc. The diagram never lets the reader forget Δ is drawn larger than physical.

Concentric clip discs drawn over the right column and the calendar bands (each ground knocked out of what lies beneath): inner ochre square tile, ring-and-dot band, a salmon band, a sawtooth ring of black triangles, each ring keylined.

A vase profile r(t) (smoothstep between knots) is mirrored into a closed polygon about the axis’ projected x, filled pink with a left-heavy horizontal density ramp; the pink floor behind the row carries a cast band.
The pixel is the weight-average of the thirteen OKLab colors; converting back to sRGB only at the end keeps the transitions out of gray.
A stripe of half-width h convolved with a gaussian is two erfs; evaluating them per pixel gives a blur whose radius follows the light with no pyramid and no second pass.

Each organ is a closed polyline built from cubics/quads, knocked out of the plates beneath, filled on its plate and keylined; asters are 15–17 two-quad petals round an ochre disc; goldenrod plumes are arcs of ochre dots with keyline crescents.

The head is one bowl in local coordinates with y scaled by cosθ: a rim ellipse, a corolla sunk toward the near side, inner rays converging from rim to corolla, and outer rays leaving the rim along its normal, so a flat rim sends a crown up and a fringe down while a top-down head reads as a full disc.

canvas fillText/strokeText on the green, dark-green, red and keyline plates (each with its own register offset); the month is a light green fill with a dark green outline like the reference’s decorated serif.
A downward triangle under tilted heads, in the head’s roll frame, filled only with cream and white dots whose density fades toward the tip; drawn after the far rays and before the near fringe.

Double-ruled square; sky plate, horizon strip, rays from a point behind the sheaf; the sheaf body is one knocked-out polygon with keyline stalks fanning through it, bound by a tan band, each stalk ending in an ear of alternating ochre grains with thin awns.

A linear gradient across the cell from the low side to the high side of its level; the direction is the discrete gradient of f, so neighboring cells chain into a continuous ramp while each one stays a square.
Cell step: one cell offset by up to 0.09 turn, so its edges show a hard change of color.
Rim bands: stripes that follow the pill's edge inside 0.07 of its height.
Three offscreen plates at device resolution are drawn onto white paper with globalCompositeOperation multiply, spot first (offset), then hatch, then key, so ink over color reads as printed overprint.

Every edge is resampled at 7 u, displaced along its normal by a 3-octave sine noise (0.9 u), then filled as a variable-width ribbon (outer + inner offset polylines, even-odd) whose width = base·(1+0.22·noise)·taper·(1+0.5·max(0,−n·light))·(1+0.35·cornerProximity), so edges facing down-left and every corner run heavier; the ink layer under every later face is erased (destination-out) so occluded lines vanish.
Open rings drawn as wavered ribbons with a 40° gap on the east, each with a thin gray stem 9 u long below.
Each cord is a sine-of-y polyline; at chosen y a cubic branch leaves it with a random outward lean, optionally forking, and a red growth is drawn at each tip.

Concentric jittered rings of cream dots at 4.2 u pitch fill the lobed outline (foreshortened by cosθ and sunk to the bowl bottom); a sparse white ring sits outside it and 1100 gaussian gold dots, densest at the middle, are rejected outside the lobe.
Cut windows reuse the chip rings: a pale-orange rim ring +1.4 u, then the black (or blue-to-black thermal) fill −1.4 u translated (+1.4,+1.4), so a light hairline sits on the top-left of every cut.
Stipple fringe: dabs in the sky color climb into the pale shape, exponential in depth, 4.4 to 7.4 px radius.

Pixels brighter than 0.60 inside the marquee form a stroke mask, opened 1 px and cleaned of components under 10 px; parts thicker than tMax 4 (an opening of radius 2, ≥ 40 px) are masses traced as marching-squares outlines at 0.9 px, the rest is Zhang–Suen thinned to one centerline per stroke, chained, spurs shorter than 1.0 × thickness dropped, and drawn at its chamfer-measured thickness clamped to [1.4, 4].

Same medial-axis pass on the raw luminance inside the screen polygon: bright game pixels > 0.20, closed 1 px, skeletonised and drawn at thickness [1.1, 4]; masses become outlines and are also written into the knock-out mask that the spot plate honors.
Right-aligned rows of 3–6 orange rectangles of random width with a 4 u gap and 11 u pitch stand in for text; nothing is typed.
One scalar per cell: how deep the cell center sits in the stroke, scaled by the same elliptical light field as ST-09, so the right side of the 9 runs to the top of the ramp and the left stays low.
Each silhouette is a vertex list with corner radii; corners are replaced by tangent-point arcs and the ring is sampled at ~3 u so the same polyline feeds fill, clip, normal offset and stroke.
The digit is the level index. It is drawn after the fill in a single ink read from the reference, lifted only on the dark green cells where it would vanish.
Salmon field, then a darker salmon plate of jittered discs on a 9.5 u hex lattice knocked out of the ground, both under the keyline.
Start cap of the upper deck: a white Archivo 700 numeral centered in a 14.25 px round cap, with the 1 px paper outline between it and the next track.
A light band 26 px wide: its edge wanders by 4.5 px σ with 4 px teeth, two flat greens and a 2 px ramp between.
The edge of the red reach cuts straight through lenses; the zone is a mask, not a feature of the wave.
The top disc's wall: solid white, 11 px tall, the lip above it narrows to a quarter of its width at the back.
Row ends at the sheet edge: the density field runs off the paper without a border.
A wall: 4 px of black keyline on each side of a 6 px gap, all from one distance value.
The front flame: a pink core in the lower 58 %, lavender at its edge, lime fringe, the wick splitting its foot.
Center: 12 yellow teeth in a zigzag around a black hole 0.36 of the ring radius, on a lilac disc with a dark collar.
Magenta facets: alternate sectors from 1 to 2.3 gem radii, crisp at a 1 px edge, cut by the hairlines.
Pebble beach: black-rimmed blue pebbles in white foam, green patches with black stipple under them.
The gap down the middle: white beads, and the inner edges of all four wings.
The margin: 11 px of bare ground, then the rows begin mid-dot.
Frisket edge: the band turns over in 1.3 px, then the glint starts
Tuft: loose ends splayed from the band edge at 55 % of the stitch width
Flying dots: rings with a center dot
Stripe edge: paper shows between key and yellow, the plates 2.5 px apart
Hand: orange plate 2 px off its key, nails in white
Star crossing: several ground arms meet at a branch point of the set; the reference arms measure 12 px median and 29 px at p90.
Cut edge: the disc color meets the ground in 1.5 px with no halo.
Shadowed top edge: it starts gray blue, 65 118 180, with no yellow or pink.
Pill edge: cut in 1.4 px, with a light line on the first 1.6 px inside.

Tangents (−gy, gx) normalized, flat pixels seeded at 45°, then two iterations of the separable Kang ETF: each tangent replaced by the weighted sum of its neighbors over ±5 px in x then y, weighted by tangent alignment and the magnitude difference through a tanh table.
Drips: columns under the type decay over 2 to 26 cells, one in three edge cells at the default.

DoG across the flow normal (σc 1.0, σs 1.6, ρ 0.985) sampled bilinearly, integrated along the ETF streamline with a σm 3 Gaussian, thresholded 1 + tanh(40 H) < 0.5, two iterations with ink fed back; non-maximum suppression across the normal keeps one ridge per edge, Zhang–Suen thins it, chains are followed with junction splitting, bridged over 3 px gaps, split clear of the structure and the marquee/screen, Douglas–Peucker simplified at 0.5 px, and weighted 0.9 (structure, thickness ≥ 2.6) or 0.6 (detail).
One vec2 uniform. Every other value on the plate is a function of r, the squeezed distance to it.
Hatch: horizontal streaking in the tone, strongest at the horizon, 46 px across and 2.6 px tall.
Warm plateau: the field held at 0.43 turn, orange 250 99 26, flat across several cells.
Each face is a closed polygon filled with one of the four hexes; the ink layer under it is erased so occluded lines vanish, then the face paints its own density before its own detail lines are drawn.
Solid orange fill through the same backing/offset machinery; no gradient, only the closing grain; a mint 1.5 u rule and 3 u dots as fittings.
Polygons filled with the plate ink at full opacity, with no gradients or tone; the keyline does all the modeling.
The slab top is filled pink, then two families of axis lines are ribbon-stroked with the ink clipped to the face polygon; later faces erase what they cover.
The S-bend: dabs fan slightly on the outside of the curve because they are spaced by arc length.
The river: rows of white packed 1.45 times tighter than the rows beside them, running the width of the plate.
The contour is offset inward and re-wavered with its own noise so the folds follow the cocoon without being parallel copies.
Colorbar: the same lookup drawn over one turn, 0 to 1, so it is the true scale of the field above.

A solid blue ellipse (58×46 u) at the leaf root, then a 900-stroke opaque band straddling the rim so the disc edge never shows, a solid #1E3CC0 core 38 u across set 12 u up the axis, then 5200 radial strokes (on a layer masked by leaf, blob and stems) starting anywhere inside the blob, each drawn as 5–11 dashes with random gaps and per-dash alpha, color running from a deep #17327C at the root to #1D4888 within the first 28 % of the reach, alpha falling (1−t)^1.8 to zero 40–180 u past the edge; the blob and its rim get 360 lighter streaks.
Frosted run: light gray with the type under it blurred 3.5 px and shown at 25 %.
The blurred coverage b, pushed through a saturating curve and mixed toward white under the stroke; faded out where σ is near zero so the crisp stroke carries no halo.
Halo above the type: 40 px veil, blue above green from 14 px out; the green glow is gone by 50 px.
Light helix: a σ 1.3 px core over a σ 3.8 px skirt, added over black

One ImageData pass over the composite multiplies R, G and B by 1 + 0.042·(0.6·n(c) + 0.2·n(c−x) + 0.2·n(c−y)) with n a signed hash on 1.385 u cells, giving mono grain with a 0.35 lag-1 correlation like the reference’s.
A hashed value per 2-px cell nudges OKLab L up or down; since it rides on L it darkens and lightens without shifting hue.
Bare ruling: rings at 6.25 px pitch, a gaussian dip of 26/255 with σ 0.6 px and a 6/255 half-pitch ring between, under 3.3/255 of grain.
Flower patch: 14 orange petal ellipses and a lilac disc laid as vertical capsule stitches, 3.5 px columns, 12 px long, red second thread on 19 % of stitches.
Open sky: specks at 8 to 12 % coverage, median 2 px, evenness 0.27 so they stand apart.
Far to the side the two trains are equal in height: a lattice of lozenges on a 14.5 by 31 px cell, black crest cores ringed white, yellow trough cores ringed black.
Inside a disc face: thin ridges under the lit lip, then the spool's speckle at 47 % coverage.
A dab tip: dots pile up to nearly solid; the rounded edge is a density edge, not a drawn one.
A green cell: the fill is decided by hash, 41 percent of cells; its grain is 1.5 times the gray's.
Deep aura: violet with pale white dots on the 5.7 px lattice.
At 4x: the pale ground is a diagonal checker of yellow and olive, the olive phase broken to yellow on an ordered lattice, 2.21 px per cell.
Halo specks at 160 px: 29 % cover in the reference, gray-green, with dark ground showing between them.
Cloud band: pink dots over blue, about half and half, thinning over 80 px into the white wedge below.
Flat green: cyan dots over yellow on one lattice, so the gaps between the cyan dots read yellow.
Where rows bunch, the dots stay round: the local frame comes from the stream function's own slope.
Floor grid, 39 px at the foot, rows closing as (y − horizon)²
Packed bar: loops 6.4 px apart with a dark groove between, 96 % coverage
Mint plate up close: σ 14 speckle, 2 px specks, no gradient
Open road: σ 6 grain smeared 1 px along the feed
Open green: σ 14 speckle leaning to light specks, grid lines every 99 px
Ground arm: the slowest 20 % of pixels, a per-pixel draw through slate, steel, periwinkle and pale; navy specks gather in 3 px rosettes where the orbit never leaves.
Mix: halfway along the ramp the mint and the red average to a dusty rose; the grain is densest here.
Interior: near-black green 1 37 5 with grain σ 0.7.
Dark band to yellow: the steepest run of the ramp, where the jittered read scatters dark specks into the yellow.
Flank: from orange down through red and magenta to violet; the dither speckle is densest here, σ 3.8.

Short 1 u strokes along each plate’s axis field (radial for fans and throat, petal-axis for lobes) in lighter and darker fill tints at α 0.32, clipped to the plate; then an ImageData pass multiplies every non-transparent pixel by 1±amp·hash(⌊x/1.6u⌋,⌊y/1.6u⌋), amp 0.07 where R>G+40 else 0.02.
White fill; the grid is stroked after every cell so the fills never cover it, which is the one thing that makes the cells read as paper squares instead of pixels.
Grid crossing: two 2 px lines that multiply the field to about 0.45 of its value.
One ImageData pass: ground color × vignette × (1 + hf + lf) per pixel.
Flat fill plus a radial 1.5 % darkening from 55 % radius to the corners; the grain pass gives it its tooth.
Flat white; the lit faces carry no tone.
Ground: flat 230 230 230; no grain reaches it.
One sawtooth polyline along the base of the side face, 3 u period and 1.7 u amplitude, drawn as a 0.6 u chain with three 60° stubs above its left end.
Two rings of filled pen dots with displaced centers and a slow radial wobble, so they are not concentric; short rays of random length inside them.
One open polyline per hand (wrist → palm → four narrow U-fingers → thumb → wrist) hanging outside the shroud, with a dash-dot palm crease.

A direction field blends the 60° plate angle toward the ETF by structure-tensor coherence (smoothstep 0.25 → 0.65; the side face is ruled, coherence ignored); tone bands from a σ4 blur assign dsep 7 / 4.5 / 3.2 px, and Jobard–Lefer evenly-spaced streamlines are traced from ridge-adjacent seeds and a 5 px lattice with a spatial-hash separation test, breaking at 30° turns, then a 60° cross pass on the darkest band; strokes are Catmull-Rom smoothed and drawn at 0.6 px.

A tone map over the side face (lighter at the top and along the front edge, darker toward the ground) sets dsep; Jobard–Lefer placement seeds only the core of the face and traces streamlines through a 60° field with ±0.5° curvature, each stopping at its own random clearance from the polygon (largest toward the front edge and the top) or at half dsep from an existing line; lines under 22 u are dropped, 8 % are split with a gap, 5 % get a short doubled companion, and each is stroked 0.82–1.0 u (thicker toward the ground) with round caps.
Hop cones rise above the salmon band as ovoid pale-yellow silhouettes carrying six rows of downward keyline bract scallops; tan lobed leaves and sage bines cross the dot screen.
Five depth samples per cell vote on whether the cell is inside the stroke, so a thin pass through a cell corner does not ink it and a cell straddling the edge does.
Shadow edge: black spray at most 0.8 dense along the underside of a lobe, 77 % black here.
Straight beaded runs from each rim point inward to the corolla edge, slightly bowed, pale blue and converging; the near wall is seen from outside so its inner rays are skipped.

Silhouette polylines are offset 1 u inward along their normals, displaced by a 3-octave 1-D sine noise of the arc length (amp 1.2 u), and stroked in 8-point segments whose width varies ±18 %; a second 3.2 u pass at α 0.55 with a faster waver frays the edges.

Every chip is a set of rings; the backing ring is offset +1.4 u along its normals and translated (+1.4,+1.4), the fill ring is offset −1.4 u and translated the same, and the plum line is stroked on the unmoved ring at 2.1 u so a pale hairline shows inside the top-left edges and outside the bottom-right ones.

Every silhouette and rule is a polyline displaced by 3-octave sine noise of arc length (amp 0.7 u) and stroked in 8-point runs whose width varies ±15 %, into one keyline canvas multiplied over the sheet last.

An edge is cut into 2–5 pieces separated by 0.8–2.4 u gaps; each piece is rotated ±0.4° about its center, shifted ±0.3 u across, wavered and drawn as a 3 u-tapered ribbon, so the line reads as a set of FDoG chains, not a rule.

Each normalized polyline is mapped into the source rect, densified every 4 u, displaced along its normal by three-octave sine noise (amp 0.15 u), and filled as a ribbon whose half-width tapers 0.25 → 1 over 8 u at free ends, so lines meet with hairline gaps instead of joints.

Each mass is rasterized on a 2-px cell grid, its cell boundary is chained into a loop and Catmull-Rom smoothed; the loop is punched out of the (offset) plate and stroked 1.15 u on the key canvas, so a blue sliver shows inside the outline on the top-left and white outside on the bottom-right.
Two rules and two antiphase zigzags make a row of diamonds with a pen dot in each; the spine verticals stop above and resume below the band.
Rim of the G: edge cells take the 2.4 display gamma, so they drive to mint one cell wide while the interior fuses to white.

An asymmetric cordate polygon per leaf is sampled on a rotated square grid; each dot’s Ø is full in the margin band, shrinks toward the middle, and smoothsteps to zero across the last 10 u inside the edge so no outline forms; a paler half-cell-offset screen is added.
Random fine dots whose keep-probability grows with depth inside the leaf and is modulated by two value-noise scales, giving the blotchy dark middle.
Each leg is a twisted cord of two sines; each foot a closed contour 34 wire px long; the comb hangs from the V hem with a sine crossing it.
Lit cap: a solid sliver 6 px thick at the median on the high ground, its glow falling 46 px down the slope as stipple.
Pale band: the reflected sky from 0.24 below the horizon to 0.9 up, fading over its bottom 0.4, brightest left of center.
A horizontal source is a parabola in u; the distance is vertical. The bow is what makes the bands rise toward the edges instead of running flat.
A Fourier-radius blob clipped to the chip fill, filled with its own low-contrast thermal ramp, then outlined with the same slipped keyline so it reads as a second cut layer of liquid.
Rec.601 luminance stretched between its 2nd and 98th percentiles, an unsharp mask of 0.6 × (L − G₈(L)), and the marquee panel z-normalized at k 2.5 so the lettering separates.

On the capsule a second, smaller-scale warped field with its own blue/pale/yellow ramp is mixed in by color where the weight rises along the length, so the right end breaks into a few soft blue and yellow pools while the left stays a smooth pink-to-white plateau.
Fringe: hairs 4 to 34 px standing off the shore edge at 1.4 px spacing, each brightest in its root half.

Skeleton strokes per glyph in a 10-unit grid are sheared 12°, wavered, stroked black at body + 2 × outline on a text canvas, then the body is erased with destination-out; the remaining ring is the mass outline the medial-axis pass draws for lettering.
A binary keep-mask rasterized from the hand-set silhouette polygon, the drop rectangle cleared, then eroded 4 px (dilate of the inverse with a disc of radius 4); nothing is drawn outside it.

Each tint plate is an offscreen canvas whose base transform is translated by its offset; a fill knocks its polygon out of the other plates, then all plates are multiplied onto a white sheet, mottled, and multiplied onto the paper.

Every mark is a polyline in wireframe px mapped to plate units, displaced along its normal by 0.9 u of 3-octave sine noise of arc length plus a 0.15 u tremor, and stroked once at 3.44 u with round caps and joins on one of the two ink canvases.
Cosine dome polygon filled flat with faint grain; the keyline is stroked from base corner to base corner over the arc and skips the base.
Disc: flat paint; its edge is the one hard edge on the sheet.
No mixed colors anywhere; every midtone in the picture is black dots over a flat ink, so the color histogram stays five-peaked.
Flat fill plus a hashed per-pixel brightness noise; nothing else is drawn on the paper except ink.
Flat cream fill with a hashed per-pixel brightness noise; nothing else is drawn on the paper except the two inks.
Flat paper: no fiber, no tint; the only texture on the sheet is the dot.
Flat sky: blue grain of 7.5 levels with about 6 % sparse white spray dots.
Ground between dots: dark gray with a 1 px speckle, about 60 % of the plate.
ImageData pass over the composited sheet: every non-white pixel is multiplied by 1 ± 0.022·hash(⌊x/cell⌋,⌊y/cell⌋); white (paper) pixels are untouched.

One iso(X,Y,Z) maps every point; boxes are three parallelograms (top, +X front, −Y return) drawn back to front, then a hexagonal silhouette contour and three inner edges from the interior vertex (X1, Y0, Z1); cylinders are the projected front arc at the base, two vertical tangents at ±1.199 r and the projected back arc at the top.
Each source is a position, an OKLab color and a reach. Its weight at a pixel is a gaussian of the distance; nothing is clamped, so every source touches every pixel a little.
Ten stacked tracks: 29.5 px ink, 1.4 px paper hairline, ten greens from (221,232,152) outward to (0,87,66) inward.
Band pitch 103.3 px from the center 68 px above the plate middle; the lumps along an edge run 20 to 27 px.
A source: its own rings dominate here, so the cut reads as clean red circles with thin black and blue lines.
The bold band: yellow where the red plate sits on the green, a thin red edge on one side and the black between.
Rows stacked: one row's tails reach the next row's tips, so the sheet reads as scales.
A channel: mint, 28 px median width, swelling along the run, with its own keyline where it passes a cell.
A flame tip: the lime tongue swings one way low and the other way high.
Gem: a 25 px blue pentagon with a violet face and a 2 px light rim; the reference measures an 18 px equivalent radius.
A wave band's gradient: dark at one edge, toward yellow at the other, as the dots of each ink grow and shrink.
Single-layer face: the ramp from the top glint through the dark fold to [254,71,24]
Satin run at 54°: the lit crown rides the 4.8 px twist, dark flanks either side
Bark: wavy lines on a 9 px pitch along the trunk
Green racer: a flat plate under the key, 3 px off
Pole: blue plate, cross bars every 22 px, the black shadow band 38 px below
Royal band: navy and royal striations every 4.6 px, every second line printed bold white where a 26 px noise allows.
Crease: an arc where the ramp starts over, rim color on the line, red reached in about 30 px on its sharp side.
Lit bottom edge of the tall slab: yellow for 5 px, pink by 12, blue by 36, dark by 72.
Six-stop ramp evaluated per pixel from m; the pink plateau and red far field are the same gradient read at its ends.
The reference’s five flat inks, in the order they occur from the edge of a stroke to its spine, become stops of a continuous OKLab ramp; level 1 sits at the first stop and level 9 at the last.

Each ray starts on the rim ellipse, heads along the ellipse normal with a 0.09 rad twist and a near-side droop, and is walked at 1 u steps; every 6.0 u of arc one solid disc is placed whose Ø and color are read from the ramp at the ray parameter.
Nine upper semicircles with per-arc radius and center jitter, stroked in red over the spine.

Beads are placed around the projected rim at 2.4 u pitch, thinned on the far side and doubled and darkened on the near side; on top-down heads 92 % of the rim beads are dropped so the rays read as one continuous fan.

Course joints and staggered verticals are ribbon lines (5 u) doubled by a 3.6 u bevel line over a sparse blue face; under each course a gradient band in the density map makes the stipple read as a chamfer; the arch is an annulus sector of yellow with radial joints over a dark stippled recess.
After compositing, one ImageData pass applies a horizontal then vertical 3-tap binomial blur so keylines and dot screens carry the reference scan’s soft edges instead of crisp anti-aliasing.

150 short random walks on a 9.8 u lattice (jittered 1.1 u) inside the glass, biased to the left ten columns, each stroked as one 3 u round-capped path with rounded corners, dots on 70 % of its nodes and a 5 u stub at the end; the top row is a dotted rule and four open-square glyphs are added; all on the plate canvas, so the holes punch them.
Knot: the top thread's crest at a crossing, its brightness drawn from an exponential tail; the strongest break through to primer.
Hot spot: small domes that climb whole turns, so each reads as rings of every color.

techniques.name: Vector spot plate, knocked out, off register

uses.implementation: Screen pixels with raw luminance ≤ 0.36 are closed 3 px and opened 2 px, the screen masses knocked out, components under 1 % of the frame dropped, then traced by marching squares (holes kept), simplified at 0.6 px, Catmull-Rom smoothed and filled evenodd in the core color with a 1 px spread trap; the plate prints 1.5 px right and 1.0 px down of the key.

The screen polygon is re-sampled every 0.58 u; the left edge is inset by a tone-shaped wedge (wide at the top, spilling into a foot at the bottom), both sides get a low-frequency wobble plus one-pixel jitter quantized to the pixel grid, the shape is filled flat blue with a 1.15 u spread trap on a canvas translated (0.86, 0.58) u, and composited under the key.
Cubic from the throat splaying outward, stroked cream; the end gets a cream disc then an olive ring.
Eleven straight red verticals; 4-point stars are 8-vertex polygons of varying radius stroked closed on the center line.
Cubic centerlines are offset ±15 u along their normals into closed ribbons, split at a parameter into black and blue fills, and keylined as one silhouette.
Teal ribbon segment under the center bloom, then 700 vertical blue strokes whose alpha rises with depth, clipped to the ribbon.

The shaft is filled blue and a horizontal gray gradient plus ten per-flute sawtooth gradients are painted into the density map inside the shaft clip; the global pass reads the map (upscaled so dots stay ≥ 2.6 px), keeps each work pixel with probability λ/dotArea and stamps an anti-aliased disc, then the dot layer is box-filtered to the plate, crisped with a smoothstep on coverage and composited as black.

Half-lit faces get a uniform 0.10–0.11 in the density map; additive (lighter) gradient bands are laid from 3-D edges with bandE(), which takes the edge and an into-face direction and builds the band perpendicular to the projected edge so its iso-lines stay parallel to the edge.
Dry-brush streak: pale paint that only reaches thread tops, gated by lattice height above 0.42.
One quadratic per ray from the fan root to the rim at angular pitch = 30 u / rim radius, clipped to the fan, then a 6.75 u teal band stroked on the silhouette before the keyline leaves a 4 u gap.
d = min over 72 segment distances, unrolled into the fragment shader at build time.

Normalized polylines drawn on the key plate as tapered ribbons (0.25 → 1 over 7 px at each free end) at 0.9 px; the pipeline rasterizes the same lines into a mask dilated 7 px and cuts its own chains wherever they touch it.
Lit petal face: beads at 180 to 220 luminance, a hot rim where the petal edge faces the upper-left light.
The stroke core is a second threshold on the same distance d, with a half-width that shrinks as the blur rises, so the needle point and the glow are one decision.

For each chip an ImageData at 1.6 u pitch evaluates f = perlin(p + warp·q) + 0.3·perlin(2p + …) with q a 2-octave warp, adds a linear ramp along the chip and an optional edge-distance term, stretches by the contrast, steepens the slope locally around one ramp value so a single liquid contour hardens, and looks the result up in a 256-entry pale-biased ramp LUT; the bitmap is drawn smoothed into the fill clip.

14000 short radial strokes at α 0.42 from the throat point, each colored by the ramp at (r ± 6 % jitter) and lightened or darkened ±14 % so the ramp is pencil-grained so the stops are ragged, over a flat coral fill; grain strokes on top.
Alternate 12 u cells filled on the black plate; keyline rules top and bottom.
Light-ochre field with paper hearts (two arcs and a point) cut out and keylined; a row of black squares alternates between heart rows.
Staggered rows of keyline semicircles (r = pitch/2) over a light-ochre field, a keyline dot at each arc center, clipped to the band; rust rule beneath.
Slate ribbon spirals every 60 u joined by a quadratic wave ribbon, each knocked out of the pale ground and keylined, black dot in the trough.

On a hex-staggered 52 u grid each spiral is an Archimedean polyline (r = 3.5 → r_max over 1.3–1.5 turns) offset along its normals into a ribbon, knocked out of the pale plate, filled slate and keylined; a black dot sits in each gap.
Ochre field with paper squares cut out (destination-out on the plate), each square keylined with a wavered outline, keyline dots on the half-pitch lattice.
Peach plate clipped to the arch, keyline star sprigs on a staggered lattice with a dot between.
Sine polylines stroked as slate ribbons on pale gray, each with a thin keyline along one edge.
A rust polyline zigzag between two rust rules, on the rust plate, over paper.
The tail: the same dots, fewer of them, with the light ink mixed in as the dark thins out.
The front candle's pool: lime at the middle where the flame lights the wax, lavender at its lip, its light spilling past the wall.
Bead chain on the pale ground: the dark phase prints indigo and the light phase lilac, inside a yellow and olive checker.
Hill top: bare yellow under the keyline, then green dots 3.2 px across thickening downhill.
The fan: wedge rays from the gap over a scalloped blob, each ray's gradient darkening outward.
The white field: whole rows of white dots, each ending at its own place as it meets the teal.
Two offscreen canvases, one per ink, each stroked with its own color; both are drawn in multiply onto the paper so crossings darken like wet ink.
Labels on their tracks: straight, tangent at the midpoint, Archivo 400 name and 700 value, cap tops 1.5 px off the leader, softened by 0.45 px σ.
The card: a 24 px corner, 88 px icon tile, 30 px cap JetBrains Mono with a 0.5 px stroke and a bright ringing halo, the layer softened by 0.35 px σ.
Headline core: cells with four lit neighbors fuse into a solid; the drive caps at Tc = 4 and every channel reads about 235 252 250.
Type: Archivo 500, 27.5 px caps, 50.5 px from baseline to baseline.
Four cubics per back petal run parallel to the petal axis from base to tip without converging; each front lobe gets four transverse quadratic ribs, olive doubled by a tan line 2.8 u below.

One cubic centerline is stroked in 4 u segments whose width is a tapered base times 1-D noise; small flecks are scattered along both edges to dry the line, and the lower run is re-stroked over the heads so the same vine passes both behind and in front.
When non-zero, the sample position is displaced by a divergence-free curl of value noise before the pulls are evaluated, so color is carried and never pinched.
Open sky: the 4 px lattice at ±16 levels, 45 % lattice and 55 % tooth, column means 99 to 116.

box() resolves a {ret:true} face spec into the yellow fill plus a uniform 0.14 and three additive edge bands laid with bandE() from the face’s own 3-D edges, so the spatter is densest against the contour and thins toward the middle of the face.
Cream flat, then a low-frequency perlin multiply, a 0.35 px blur for the scan, then mono grain over everything including the inks.
Each strand is a quadratic curve from the hub. Its control point lies on the bundle’s ray at trunk × reach; its end is turned from that ray by the curl plus its share of the spread.
uses.limits: trunk under ~0.25 lets strands separate at the hub and the bundle reads as a plain fan. Past ~24 bundles the sheet fills and single arcs stop reading.

uses.implementation: ψ decides where the isoclinics fall. The domain warp bends the sheet — the plates are not flat starbursts — and warping θ makes lanes of unequal width; neither breaks the physics because δ and ψ are still evaluated from one coordinate.
A white box, then random-width dark bars from a seeded sequence; the digit row is mono type below the bars.
Each shape is stroked twice on the black plate: 2.2 u on the path, then 1.4 u on the path shifted by a seeded 0.6 u jitter, which thickens the line unevenly.
Four Fourier-radius blobs are filled with a radial white-to-gray gradient on a black canvas (union by lighten) at one-third resolution, blurred with σ = 46 u and read back as a 0..1 luminance field.
uses.limits: Under σ ~15 u the edge profile is too steep for the ramp and the bands alias. Past σ ~110 u neighboring blobs fuse and the rim stop no longer closes. harmonic_scale above ~2 makes r(θ) cross zero and the outline self-intersects.

uses.implementation: Each panel is a union of rectangles (spine, face, flap, tab, rounded tuck) tested per pixel; the fill is the board color mixed 3 % toward the scuff color by a perlin mottle and a vertical shade, plus sparse one-pixel dots.
Capsules point outward from a circle. Length and width follow a sine with three lobes around the dial; ink follows the angle through the five bands.
uses.limits: Over ~120 spokes the inner ends overlap into a ring. lobes at 0 gives a plain sun.

uses.implementation: Each rung is a vertical capsule whose length is 2 × amplitude × |sin φ|. Two dots sit at its ends; the near strand’s dot is 45 % larger and the far one 45 % smaller.
uses.limits: Over ~90 rungs the capsules touch and the helix reads as a ribbon. Under one turn there is no crossing and it reads as a lens.

uses.implementation: Each icon is two to eight straight round-cap strokes on a 2 × 2 unit square; the last stroke takes an ink.
uses.limits: stroke above ~10 u closes the gaps in the sun and the helix.

uses.implementation: Each column is filled top to bottom with capsules whose length and width follow the column’s position t on the growth axis; lengths vary ±50 %. A column repeats every panel height, so the fall loops.
uses.limits: Pitch under ~4 u turns the late columns into a solid tint. gap under ~0.1 fuses a column into a bar. A lean past ±30° crosses three columns and the axis stops reading.

uses.implementation: Button, toggle, three chips, slider, pager and a nine-bar meter are all one rounded bar at different sizes, filled or outlined. The meter reads the slider value.
uses.limits: Under 24 u height the 11.5 u label touches the pill edge.

uses.implementation: One caption centered under each object on the black plate; a sheet title at the top and a folio at the foot.
Three short captions in Inter at 22 u, set flat under the grain so the grain sits on the type too.
The helix canvas is masked by an elliptical radial gradient so glyphs fade out toward the middle; the title sits in the hole with a wide dark text-shadow that deepens it.

Each word is filled three times in #FF0000, #00FF00, #0000FF with globalCompositeOperation lighter on a transparent layer, offset per channel; where all three overlap the sum is white, at the edges one or two channels show; the layer is drawn under the chrome.
Characters are placed as a field: a spiral of letters, an ellipse of marks.
Characters are placed as a field: a spiral of letters, an ellipse of marks.

A quarter-resolution copy of the picture is blurred; its luminance is added to the line phase, so lines rise over light forms and sink into dark ones. The same pass stores blurred edge energy for the guilloche mask.
uses.limits: flow · amp_pitches · pitch must stay under ~1.5 × radius or neighboring lines fold over each other at hard edges.

uses.implementation: Counts are drawn as bars in two or three greens, with a dashed baseline for the expected value.

Tone is printed as a count of one-pixel dots per cell, so density carries the value and nothing is blended; two screens multiplied make the rings.
Faint diagonal strokes in the scuff color on a separate layer, blurred 1.5 px, then composited so the edges are soft.
Nothing is shaded: depth is the alpha ramp and the projected font size, so far glyphs are ghosts and near glyphs are ink.
A soft multi-stop gradient fills a card cut to an arch, a step or a notch; a large number sits in the cut.

line 1 is sized to 924 u (font-stretch is set after ctx.font, which resets it); the figure sits on line 2 flush right; the slab is drawn after the type so it covers the bottom of the headline as the reference slab does.
Tone is the larger of a soft core disc and the nearest ray. A ray is a gaussian across its axis whose width tapers to the tip.
uses.limits: Over ~60 rays, or a root width above ~140 u, the rays merge into a disc. core_radius at 0 leaves the rays unjoined.

A mid-tone is the plate ink drawn as a regular dot grid clipped to the shape; the dot radius is set from the requested coverage.
band = exp(−((|n.z|−0.34)/0.06)²) mixes the edge color in; spec = (n·h)^60 mixes white in; both read from the same normal buffer as the LUT.
All lettering is live type in the three inlined fonts with invented plain words; spine text is drawn on a rotated context.

A chamfer distance transform gives d to the silhouette; dc is the distance to the nearest convex corner or fold junction and df to the spine crease or flap fold. A pixel turns lighter where a uniform random is below the summed density times the patch gate, so the wear reads as clustered abrasion rather than a line.

Distance to the nearest line center is compared with half the tone-set width and antialiased over one device pixel. In the highlights each line is cut into dashes whose fill falls with darkness, with a hashed offset per line.
uses.limits: Under ~2.5 device px of pitch the lines alias into tone. duty_max · weight at 1 closes the shadows to solid ink and the crosshatch has nothing to cross.

ART.grain multiplies RGB by 1 + 0.10·n per channel (visible on the chrome and the type); a second pass adds signed noise of 14/255 so the black ground carries grain too, as film does.

One pass over the whole canvas after every panel is drawn: a mono additive noise scaled down with luminance (it reads in the black, thins in the pink), plus a small per-channel multiplicative term for the color speckle.
Multiplicative hashed noise, identical across channels.
Capsules are drawn into a coverage layer per ink. Each pixel of the layer is then set fully on or off: on when a random number is under coverage × density.
uses.limits: edge above ~1.5 u dissolves the smallest capsules. density under ~0.5 reads as a tint, not as ink.

uses.implementation: Site lattice at the pitch (CSS px), jittered. Value field (linear · radial · noise) eased from → to. Screen: FM keeps a site when its blue-noise rank < value; AM keeps every site with radius ∝ √value; the dial interpolates. The mask is sampled at the site, so dots are whole or absent. Each dot is geometry: a signed distance to an irregular nib outline (7 vertex radii), so its edge is always 1 device px of anti-aliasing, never a blur. The stock edits the edge: the distance is displaced by the stock height (edge rag), valleys inside the dot can starve, fibers wick a short way out. Film τ = thickness × pressure. Color: Beer–Lambert film in linear light (or a coverage mix). Ink B overprints by the same film product. Light last: × the stock's shading under the sheet light.
uses.limits: pitch < 1.2 px: sites merge into flat tone at 1×: the stipple stops reading as marks. dot radius < .3 px: below ~½ device px at 1× a dot is a gray pixel, not a mark. dot radius > ½ pitch: dots fuse into a solid; FM loses its range. edge rag > .9 px: dots read as fuzz, not ink. selection white: clumps and voids at low density

uses.implementation: Pressure = dropoff curve of the signed distance to a warped edge line (stroke direction, transition width), × the mask. Ink chain: the stock height under the inked area (blended with film-splitting noise, clumped and streaked along the stroke) is ranked to percentiles; pressure P inks exactly the top P of the surface, peaks first. Starve: valleys below the threshold never take ink. Wick: fibers carry ink past the edge. Mottle: paper formation thins the film. Film thickness thins with pressure unless the film breaks up; color = Beer–Lambert film in linear light. Light last: × the stock's shading. The ink sits in the tooth, not on top of it.
uses.limits: transition < 4 px: reads as a hard vector edge: no run-out to see. break-up < .3: the edge becomes a gradient: the "AI gradient" failure. stock bite < .3: speckle stops following the paper and reads as digital dither. streak > 6: marks read as scanlines unless the angle is off-axis

uses.implementation: Warp columns and weft rows at their own counts (threads / 100 CSS px); each thread: jittered center, thickness, dye-lot L, fray length, accent. Interlacing decides the top thread per crossing; a float is the run where it stays on top. Height = cylinder across the thread × arch along the float; under-threads sit low; hair = fine noise along the thread. Albedo in OKLab: under-thread, then top thread by AA coverage; accent as flecks (single floats, as in the source) or whole threads. Light: Lambert from the height gradient + a height-field shadow march toward the sheet light, so floats shade into the gaps; ambient occlusion darkens the gaps. Cut: the mask's signed distance plus each thread's own fray length, so threads end raggedly, not on a line. The swatch casts onto the page.
uses.limits: count > 50 /100 px at 1×: threads under 2 CSS px alias against a 1× display: moiré (fine on 2×/3×). count < 18 /100 px: threads over ~5 px read as a woven-texture graphic, not cloth. fill < .5: reads as a grid of strokes, not cloth. fill > .97: gutters close; the weave flattens to a check. accent rate > .15: accents stop being accents

uses.implementation: Hatch strokes along an angle at a spacing; extra layers cross at an offset angle and only print where the value field asks for more tone. Each stroke is a wobbling polyline with pressure tapering at both ends, rasterized as AA capsules (lead width). Ink chain: pressure vs stock-height percentile. The lead touches peaks first; valleys stay white. Graphite is an opaque OKLab mix, not a film. Sheen: normals from the stock relief plus the graphite deposit's own burnish texture; Blinn specular toward the sheet light, gated by how much graphite is there. Light last: diffuse × stock shading, + specular.
uses.limits: spacing < 1.2 px: strokes merge into flat gray. sheen > .8 at low light: strokes read as wet ink, not graphite. lead > 1.6 px: reads as charcoal / marker

uses.implementation: Die = an invented mark (compass, sun, crescent, knot, monogram), a word, or a ring seal, rasterized as an AA clip on the main thread (fonts). Die profile from the signed distance to the die edge (exact distance transform): a crisp shoulder, a straight wall over the die softness, a flat floor; lip = a narrow ridge just outside the edge. Height (CSS px) = stock height × (1 − crush · profile) − depth · profile + lip. The tooth flattens on the floor. Light: Lambert from the combined height + a height-field shadow toward the sheet light (the wall on the light side falls in shadow). Optional ink on the floor (film), so blind → letterpress is one dial.
uses.limits: depth > 2 px: reads as a carved gouge, not a deboss. die softness < .3 px: walls alias. die softness > 5 px: the edge goes mushy. light elevation > 70°: a blind deboss vanishes under overhead light, by design

uses.implementation: Text in Courier Prime (a typewriter slab; bold below 15 px, as a light strike loses thin strokes), one strike per glyph on the main thread: pressure = ribbon life (exhausting along the page) × key variance; offset, rotation, an occasional dropped baseline; a half strike is a linear pressure ramp across the glyph, fading top or bottom. Ribbon: a plain weave at the ribbon count. Ink transfers through thread crossings, less through the gaps. Ink chain: pressure × ribbon vs stock-height percentile; ink squash pools film at the glyph edge. Impression: the strike dents the stock (blurred glyph × pressure); light from the combined height. Color: Beer–Lambert film.
uses.limits: ribbon count < 30 /100 px: weave reads as a screen pattern on the type. jitter > 1.5 px: reads as broken font rendering. size < 7 px: strokes thinner than the tooth lose the ribbon texture

uses.implementation: Die = the same shapes as FX-06; foil lands on the AA die × the stock: valleys below the starve height release no foil (pinholes), edge flash breaks the boundary at the film-split scale. Height = stock relief × (1 − crush) + foil grain (fine crumple) − a slight deboss; normals from it. Metal: a perspective viewer above the plate; the mirror vector per pixel samples the studio: a round soft box at the sheet light, a dim ceiling and a dark room. The reflection sweeps across the foil; tight Blinn glints are added; holo rotates the hue by the reflection direction. Off-foil paper keeps its own light.
uses.limits: gloss < 6: reads as metallic paint, not foil. foil grain > .6 px: crinkled, like a chocolate wrapper. light elevation > 75°: foil goes dark: metal reflects away from an overhead light

uses.implementation: Motif = an invented mark, a word or a ring seal (AA clip, main thread) → exact signed distance. Coverage pattern: solid, or an analytic line / dot screen intersected with the motif (or with the sheet around it), so every line and dot keeps a 1-device-px edge. Film profile from the signed distance: a rounded shoulder (1 − (1 − d / rounding)²) rising to the film build. The film levels the FX-03 tooth: its top = lerp(tooth, smoothed tooth, leveling × profile) + build × profile. Stock: FX-03's relief and fibers under a board color (OKLCH; dark by default). Matte = Lambert from FX-03 × albedo + a weak, broad rough-dielectric sheen on the tooth facets. Film: Fresnel (n = 1.5, F₀ = .04) from a perspective viewer above the plate; the mirror vector samples the studio (a rectangular soft box at the sheet light, a dim ceiling, a dark room); gloss sets the box edge softness and the glint exponent. uses.implementation: Motif → exact signed distance. Satin: centerlines across the motif at the stitch angle, one per 100 / stitch count px; each centerline is marched against the motif to find where the needle goes in and out (concave motifs give several floats per row). Ends stagger (alternating needle points + jitter); floats longer than the max split into rows at brick-staggered points. Each float: a capsule whose cross-section is rounded (flatter when long), sinking into its needle hole at both ends, with an S-twist ridge along it. Floats are z-buffered by height (neighbors overlap like real satin); an optional split, running or chain stitch is traced along the motif edge (marching-squares contour, real arc length) and laid on top. Cloth (FX-04 live): pucker ridges run along the pull direction at the stitch ends, decaying away from the edge; a crease dimples just outside the satin; needle holes darken it. Its own lighting is kept and multiplied by the pucker's Lambert. Thread light: Lambert on the thread normals + an anisotropic gleam (Kajiya–Kay along the twisted filament direction × a lobe across the cylinder), from the sheet light; a height-field shadow and cavity occlusion from the stitched relief fall onto the cloth and between floats. Color: OKLCH.
uses.limits: stitch count > 45 /100 px: threads under ~2 px: the fill reads as a smooth sheet at 1× (fine at 2×+). stitch count < 12 /100 px: gaps open between floats. max float > 200 px: floats too long to hold: they would snag; read as a ribbon. sheen > .9 with low twist: reads as plastic. pull > .7: the ground reads crumpled, not stitched

uses.implementation: Coating = brush strokes in stroke space (along s, across t): a load that runs out along the stroke; edges displaced by per-side noise (raggedness); a set-down pool and a drying rim; bristle streaks × the stock height decide where a dry brush still deposits. Thickness τ = load × unevenness (streaks + low-frequency drag) + pools; overlapping strokes add (a double coat prints deeper); paper valleys hold more sensitizer. Objects (procedural fern frond, grass with spikelets, or a cut-card motif) are an AA clip. Lift = a smooth field × the lift dial; contact sets how much lies flat. Shadow: for each lift level z the clip is sampled toward the sheet light at z · cot(elevation) (smeared ±20 % along the light) and blurred by z × sky scatter; each pixel blends the two levels around its lift. Exposure E = 1 − shadow × (1 − translucency). Develop: r = ((1 − e^(−2.2·exposure·E)) ÷ (1 − e^(−2.2)))^1.35, capped at 1.2; the coat saturates as τ' = 1.3·(1 − e^(−τ/1.3)); density = τ' × (a faint stain + r) × film density. Overexposure fills the penumbra in. Wash: unexposed coating rinses away; Prussian blue bleeds a little downhill into the whites, in streaks. Color = Beer–Lambert film of the tone (fresh, classic, peroxide-oxidized, tea-toned). Light last: × the stock's shading under the sheet light.
uses.limits: object lift > 18 px: penumbra wider than the leaflets: the fern dissolves into a cloud. exposure > 2.5: penumbra fills in; fine pinnules and awns vanish. exposure < .5: pale, greenish print: reads as underexposed. raggedness > .8: stroke edges tear into islands. strokes > 6: brush marks shrink into stripes

uses.implementation: Scan lines at the pitch (≥ 2 device px), at the scan angle. Dose at a pixel = Σ over nearby lines of power ÷ speed × the beam's gaussian, integrated over the pixel (erf): anti-aliased lines at any angle. When the pitch clamps to 2 device px, the dose is scaled by the clamp so the tone matches a finer screen. Firing gate = the motif clip sampled at each line's centerline, softened by the spot along the scan; the head's turnaround adds dose just inside the edges it reverses at. Defocus widens σ and lowers the peak (same energy, larger spot): paler, softer, lines merging. A power ramp can run across the raster. Char = 1 − e^(−k·(dose − threshold)) → an OKLab ramp tan → brown → black, multiplied into the stock albedo (fibers char darker). Heat halo = the dose spread a few px, browning fibers first. Relief: ablation sinks the surface with dose; the tooth is burned smooth; a fine char crust. Lit by the sheet light (grooves catch it on one wall). Vector cut: a kerf along the motif outline (offset) or a tag; tabs leave bridges. The kerf opens onto the ground below, shaded by the card edge toward the light; its walls are charred.
uses.limits: line pitch < 2 device px: clamped: finer lines alias into moiré on screen (dose is conserved). power ÷ speed > 1.4: char goes black and ablates; line structure survives only in the relief. defocus > .7: reads as a smudge, not a laser. halo reach > 9 px: reads as a scorch accident rather than a mark. kerf > 3 px: a slot, not a laser cut

150 particles climb a helix (0.018 of the height per second) while the helix turns (0.22 rad/s); each is projected through a pinhole at 800 u and drawn as text, far to near.
Each animation reads its marks from a short ordered list by index, so the field is typeset from a vocabulary rather than drawn from shapes; the helix list mixes 10 marks with 13 three-digit numbers.
Bars ranked longest to shortest in gold, black and gray, one color per intent.

Every pixel of the field is replaced by LUT[field]; the ramp is the only place color enters, so all four colorways share one field.
uses.limits: The ramp is read at 256 levels; contrast above ~2 leaves fewer than 6 levels across the rim and it stair-steps. A shift past ±0.15 moves the paper stop into the blobs or the core out of range.

uses.implementation: The tone field is sampled at quarter size. Each pixel of the bank takes the wash color with a chance equal to tone × amount, so the gradient is made of single pixels.
uses.limits: At amount 1 the wash hides the dots on light banks. grain at 0 gives a smooth gradient, which reads as blur beside the dots.

uses.implementation: Flat gray fill, then verticals and both diagonal families stroked in the grid ink at 16 % before any plate lands.
uses.limits: Above alpha ~0.35 the grid competes with the keyline. Under a 14 u pitch the three line families merge into a gray tint.

uses.implementation: Two families of stacked sine lines, mirrored, give the braided cells. Vertical distance is divided by √(1 + slope²) so line width stays even on the steep parts. The mask is (above upper_v) × (edge energy low); the straight lines fade by the same mask.
uses.limits: curvature above ~3 makes the wave steeper than the antialiasing estimate holds; pitch near the main pitch makes the hand-over at upper_v invisible.

uses.implementation: The clip path of a panel is stroked once over the field.
uses.limits: Above ~3 u the frame competes with the capsules.

uses.implementation: Inside the letter mask a dark base is laid first; then a 45° dot lattice is walked and each dot is drawn with radius and color taken from the texture value at its center, so light patches of the texture become large tan dots.
The shadow side of a shape is clipped and crossed by 45° lines at a 6 u pitch with a 12/4 dash whose phase changes per line; drawn on the black plate so it never slips.

uses.limits: tolerance + feather above ~90° keys most warm pictures whole; min_sat under ~8 % keys neutral grays by their noise hue.

uses.implementation: Before coloring, coverage is multiplied by a blurred copy of itself so fills thin toward their edges, and by a slow perlin mottle; after coloring ART.grain runs mono on the plate and paper pixels are reset to white.

Each pool has an ink, a center, a gaussian radius and a mode. Its strength is 2.4 × the gaussian, read per pixel and clipped at 1, so the middle of a pool is solid; the mode says which shape of the cell it colors.
uses.limits: size above ~2 merges the pools into one field and no region reads. gain under ~0.4 leaves only the stray pixels.

uses.implementation: Each object is a top-face mask drawn in the plane transform; a column scan drops every boundary pixel whose +x or +y probe is empty by the depth, labeling right or left face, top always winning; later objects overwrite earlier ones.
uses.limits: The drop is a column scan, so a depth past the gap to the object below it paints over that object’s top face. Shapes thinner than 4 px have no interior for the ±2 px probe and get no side faces.

uses.implementation: Multiplies the whole image; the black wedges are not masks but extinction where the material axis is parallel to the polarizer. Spinning β sweeps them around the focus.

Inside the top faces the pink plate is full except where an fbm field crosses zero: the core of the band is paper, the rim half-coverage, which reads as swirls.
uses.limits: core ≥ rim removes the half-tone rim and the veins go hard-edged. Above scale ~100 u a top face holds less than one vein. One octave gives smooth contour lines, not marble.

uses.implementation: A scale, an envelope and a stamp drawn in flat color from measured proportions.
Each meridian is an ellipse with the sphere radius as its tall axis and radius·|sin λ| as its wide one, stroked with a 6 on 5 dash.
uses.limits: Over ~31 meridians the dashes of neighbors align into bands. A radius under half the sheet height shows the sphere outline.

uses.implementation: For every δ from 0 to 1599 nm the transmitted spectrum sin²(πδ/λ)·S(λ) is integrated against the color-matching functions; the 1600 colors are the LUT the field is shaded with. Order 1 (0–560 nm) is where the plates live: black → gray → warm white → amber → orange → red; the mauve and blue of 560–700 are the cool lanes.
Each color plate is composited with its own down-right offset before the black plate lands in register, so fills open a paper sliver on the top-left of the line and spill past it bottom-right.

Each plate canvas is drawn translated by its own vector; the keyline sits on all three plates, so the offsets show as colored fringes on every edge and the overprint of all three is the near-black line.
uses.limits: Past ~8 u a plate leaves its keyline and reads as a second drawing. With all three offsets equal there is no fringe and the print reads as flat digital color.

uses.implementation: Multiplying the two gratings gives a dot lattice where both are high and long beat fringes where their phases drift; nothing is drawn as a dot — the lattice is the product.
uses.limits: knee_lo ≥ knee_hi inverts the smoothstep. gamma below ~0.8 fills the lattice to a flat tint; above ~2.5 the dots shrink to specks.

uses.implementation: Square markers sit on bundle ends and on seeded free points; each carries a seeded number set up and to the right.
uses.limits: Over ~60 nodes the labels overlap. Type under 9 u is unreadable at 900 px.

uses.implementation: Multiplicative mono grain per device pixel, then a low-frequency perlin mottle, both on the whole sheet including the blobs.

uses.implementation: Before the perforation punch the stamp layer is multiplied by a low-frequency fbm and then by ART.grain, so both tooth and mottle follow the stamp and stop at the bites.

uses.limits: Above ~0.08 either one competes with the dots.

uses.implementation: The stamp is painted as a rectangle on its own layer, then a circle at every pitch step along all four edges is punched out with destination-out; the punched layer is the clip for everything on the stamp.

Each family is one expression for δ. The sheet keeps δ in the orange-red most of the time (shape 2.4 dwells near d0) and dips to white or peaks to blue briefly; the load family is real plane-stress mechanics; the conoscopes are the textbook interference figures.

The darkest stop sits just under the mid-point of the blurred edge, where the profile is steepest, so it occupies few pixels and reads as a drawn outline; the blue halo is the ramp segment just outside it.
uses.limits: from must stay below to, and both inside 0.41–0.53 (the stops on either side). A band wider than ~0.07 reads as a dark fill, not an outline.

uses.implementation: The distance from the cell center is a superellipse. Three shapes are read from it: the solid cell, an outline band, and the gutter past it.
uses.limits: cell_at above gutter_at removes the stock band between a cell and its gutter. edge above ~0.2 thins every shape to a haze.

uses.implementation: g(p) = 0.5+0.5·cos(2π·|p−c|/pitch) for each grating; the floor keeps a base blue coverage so the field never drops to paper.
uses.limits: Pitches within ~4 u of each other push the beat fringe past the sheet; equal pitches collapse the moiré to one ring set. Below ~30 u the rings alias into the screen.

uses.implementation: Per pixel: solve q, the peak height of the arc through the pixel (three fixed-point steps, since the peak x depends on q); darkness = envelope(q) × a thresholded cosine of q whose threshold rises as the envelope falls, so the stripes thin to points where the window cuts off on the right; light stripes sit at the opposite phase. The layer is blurred 3.3 u.

The title is drawn once into a mask canvas rotated −90° about its start point; the halftone is composited through it with destination-in, then the result is drawn on the stamp layer under the perforation clip.
Two 1 u ink rules across the sheet; the caption is set right-aligned 12 u under the first rule, the two-line studio label under the second.
uses.limits: Rules under 1 device px are drawn at 1 px. A caption past ~22 u collides with the second rule’s label on a narrow sheet.

uses.implementation: A bank is a row of circles along a spine plus the area under the spine. The depth of a point is its distance inside the nearest lobe; the shading reads that depth.
uses.limits: spacing above ~1.9 opens gaps between lobes and the edge reads as beads. R_var above ~0.6 makes single lobes swallow their neighbors.

Every glyph with i mod 18 = 7 is replaced by the next palette name, set in its lifted on-ink color at weight 500 with a depth-scaled glow; the animation names its own system.

Rim banks: tone = floor + (1 − floor)·exp(−depth / rim depth). Body banks: tone = smoothstep(depth) × wisp, where wisp is three-octave noise sampled in coordinates turned to the bank and stretched along it.
uses.limits: wisp_mix at 0 leaves only the depth ramp and the banks read as flat steps. stretch above ~6 turns wisps into stripes.

uses.implementation: A second, unwarped line set whose width ramps from 0 at start to duty_max · strength at full darkness; the two sets are combined as 1 − (1−a)(1−b).
uses.limits: start under ~0.35 puts hatch into the midtones and the picture reads as a net, not an engraving.

uses.implementation: A field is drawn through a clip path. Three erasing strokes along the path then lower coverage toward the edge; the stipple turns that ramp into single pixels.
uses.limits: A feather above ~20 u erodes a third of a narrow panel. On flat fields the ramp would show as a gray band, so it is off there.

uses.implementation: A mono multiply grain over the finished sheet.
uses.limits: Above ~0.06 the grain shows inside the flat inks.

uses.implementation: Each pixel is sampled at its own position minus every pull vector times exp(−d² / r²). The grid is read at the sample point, so the sheet stretches behind a pull and bunches ahead of it.
uses.limits: A pull folds the sheet when 0.86 × vector length exceeds its radius; at strength 1 the largest ratio is 0.65. Pitch under ~24 u puts a cell below ten pixels and the outline closes.

One dot per lattice cell, moved by up to 0.42 of the pitch, with one random threshold. A dot is drawn when its threshold is under the tone at its position.
uses.limits: radius above ~0.45 × pitch merges dots into a tint. jitter 0 shows the lattice as rows. Below 3 u pitch the sheet carries over 150 k dots.

For each device pixel: blue if r1 < blue_coverage, red if r2 < red_coverage; both → overprint; neither → paper tint. A 0.6 px blur softens the pixel edges the way the reference’s scan does.
uses.limits: soften above ~1.5 px dissolves the lattice into tone; cell_px is fixed at 1 in this rebuild (a coarser cell needs a hash per cell, not per pixel).

uses.implementation: Per pixel: ink if a random number is under the coverage, with the ink drawn in proportion to each pool’s share; otherwise stock, or a stray ink pixel.
uses.limits: stray above ~0.25 lifts the stock to a tint. Any soften above 0 turns the pixels into tone and the print reads as blurred.

uses.implementation: A linear gradient from the hub to the strand end colors each strand through three inks; strands are composited with the lighter blend.
uses.limits: With both alphas at 1 on a dark ground the whole trunk clips to white.

uses.implementation: One sequence of colored stripes is crossed with itself at right angles; where warp and weft cross, their colors mix, so the check comes from the weave, not from interference.
Luminance is exposed and stretched about mid-gray before it sets any line width, so paper and solid shadow are reached inside the picture, not only at its extremes.
uses.limits: Contrast above ~2 clips most of the sheet to paper or solid line; the swelling line then reads as a two-level threshold.

uses.implementation: Sky, ridge, headland and sea are evaluated per pixel from seeded Perlin noise; tower, sheds and boat are drawn as flat lit/shadow faces on top. The function returns a canvas; every later technique only reads it.
uses.limits: Any RGB picture works in its place. Pictures with no smooth area above upper_v show no guilloche; pictures with no pixel inside the hue range print as one ink.

uses.implementation: Capitals in JetBrains Mono, set letter by letter with 0.22 em added; a short rule sits one gap below the last line.
uses.limits: Tracking above ~0.4 em breaks words into letters at this size.

uses.implementation: Each panel starts as a canvas linear gradient; C runs from the panel top-left along 66° from horizontal, with knee stops so black holds to 0.15 and pink holds from 0.67.
A 70 × 8 grid where one sine phase picks both the glyph (from a five-step ramp) and the alpha (by distance to a sine centerline), so a two-wavelength band of laminar glyphs rolls across the frame.
The filled height is floor + (1 − floor)·t^power from the bottom; a few capsules are allowed past the edge.
uses.limits: floor at 1 fills the panel and the wedge is gone. scatter above ~0.4 hides the wedge edge.
